Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
Kenneth reported three problems with the JusPrin Agent pane: the setup card's title (the print's purpose) and headline (the agent's plan) don't change, and when a model file arrives, the first message under the card reads out of place. On 2026-10-26 another session reproduced all three on jusprin-newui at 889d28681c, running a separate JusPrin instance on a copy of Kenneth's data folder: Opus 5.5 for a new 3MF opened as a new project, and Sonnet 5.5 for two imports into an existing project. Its diagnosis has three causes. First, the title and headline come only from `setup_record`, which records only a purpose the person stated, so a chat that starts by opening a file falls back to a preset name. Second, the purpose and plan belong to the chat, nothing updates them when the plate's contents change, and the plan's reassessment mark goes only to the model. Third, the chat hides the file-open event, so the agent appears to start talking on its own about a moment the pinned card no longer shows. Kenneth judged this not the best experience and wants options before any fix. A separate slice stuck at 80% during the Sonnet run is out of scope.

Task:
Brainstorm the best user experience for the JusPrin Agent pane's setup card and for the first message after a file is opened or imported. This is a design brainstorm, not an implementation: write no code.

Start by reading the reproduction report `card-headline-repro/REPORT.md` (untracked, in the main checkout at /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin) and its screenshots and saved chats in that folder. Then read the code it names:
- `AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` and its `setupPresentation`: how the card's title, headline and state label are chosen.
- `card_context` and `on_file_loaded` in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp`.
- The `setup_record` description in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`.
- `AgentUI/src/skills/file-loaded/SKILL.md`.
- `bubble()` in `AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx`, which hides the file-load note.

All of these live under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Also read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` and the "Opening and importing files" section of `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md`. The current design lives in the Claude Design System and "JusPrin v2" canvas artifacts; Figma is out of date and must not be used.

Questions to answer, each with two or three concrete options, their trade-offs and a recommendation:
1. What should the card's title and headline say before the person has stated a purpose? Today the title is the process preset name and there is no headline.
2. Should recording a plan require a purpose the person stated?
3. What should the card do when the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan? Today it keeps both, still says "Confirmed", and ignores the app's own `needs_reassessment` mark on the plan.
4. How should the chat show the event that started it (a file opened as a new project, or one imported), and how should the opening message relate to the pinned card that always shows the current setup? Today the open has no row, the opening message repeats what the card shows, and it goes stale under the card.
5. How long should the opening message be, and what should it leave to the card?

Done means a short design note: the problems in plain words, the options and the recommendations, each tied to the evidence. Include rough sketches (ASCII or a small artifact) of the card and the top of the chat for a new file and for an import. Leave the note untracked at the repository root, and say which decisions are Kenneth's to make.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_2de2e6c1-23a6-4996-a857-eb1b9dc71df1
I'll start by reading the reproduction report, the saved chats and screenshots, then the code and docs it names, before writing the design note.

# Setup card and opening-message problems: reproduction report

2026-10-26, jusprin-newui at 889d28681c (RelWithDebInfo build from 04:41 today).

The setup card at the top of the Agent pane shows a title (the purpose the person stated) and a headline (the agent's printing plan). Every problem below reproduced in a second JusPrin instance running on a copy of Kenneth's JusPrin2 data folder. The copies are deleted because they held API keys. The screenshots and saved chats are in this folder.

- **Case (a), a new model file opened as a new project:** `~/Downloads/petg-pla+support+interface.3mf`, made for an A1 preset. Opened with the Kobra 3 selected, on the default model, Claude Opus 5.5. Chat: `repro-project-opus/`.
- **Case (b), models imported into an existing project:** `find_my_hollow.3mf` was opened first; its opening message ran on Opus 5.5. I then switched the chat to Claude Sonnet 5.5 and imported `AMS_disconnect_tool_raised_letters.stl` and later `Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl` with File › Import. Chat: `repro-project/`.

## Case (a): a new model file opened as a new project

**A1. The title and headline stay empty until the person states a purpose.** After the file opened, the card's title was the process preset name, "0.20mm Standard @BBL A1", with no headline (`opus-1-opened.jpg`). It stayed that way after I picked the printer, although the agent had confirmed the printer and two filaments by then (`opus-2-after-printer.jpg`).

They changed only after I wrote "It's part of my kid's Halloween costume, so it should flex without snapping". Opus then called `setup_record`, and the title became "Kid's Halloween arrow headband that flexes without sna…" with the headline "Headband alone in PETG, flat, solid-wall band, no supports". The rule behind this is in the `setup_record` description (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`): the agent may record only a purpose the person stated, and every call must include one. A chat where nobody states a purpose never gets a title or a headline. Kenneth's 2026-10-21 chat, the source of the original screenshot, is such a chat.

**A2. The opening message reads out of place under the card.** It is the first thing in the chat, and nothing above it says a file was opened. The file-load note is drawn as nothing whenever the agent is set up: `bubble()` in `AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx`.

The card always shows the current setup, but the message keeps describing the moment the file opened. After the purpose turn, the card read "Kid's Halloween arrow headband… · Headband alone in PETG · ~1h 05m · 23 g". Directly under it, the opening message still discussed the test square, the two materials and the temperature conflict, and asked "Which printer will you print this on?" All of those had been settled (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`). The find_my_hollow opening in case (b) has the same mismatch (`sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

**A3 (minor). The card cuts off the title.** The purpose may be up to 60 characters, but the card shows a single line, so this title ended in "sna…".

## Case (b): a model imported into an existing project

**B1. The card keeps the previous print's purpose and headline.** I stated the purpose "Halloween headband costume for my kid", and Sonnet recorded it with the headline "P1S PLA, sturdier walls for the clip, arrow and tool on separate plates". I then imported `Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl`, which is unrelated to the headband. Both stayed the same.

Sonnet wrote that its "earlier plan… needs another look now that this sheet is here", but it didn't call `setup_record` (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). The purpose and plan belong to the chat, and nothing resets them when a model is imported.

**B2. The app knows the plan is out of date, but the card doesn't show it.** The saved chat's plan has `validity: "needs_reassessment"` and `invalidatedBy: "Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl"`, yet the card still said "Confirmed". The flag reaches only the model (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:92`). `card_context` in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` sends the card only the purpose and the headline.

**B3. Imports get a row in the chat; the file that opened the project gets none.** Each File › Import shows a change row, "Import Object: <file> · you · <time>", above the agent's reply. The file that created the project gets nothing, so its message has no visible trigger (see A2).

## Side issue: a slice stuck at 80% blocked plate layout

This happened in the Sonnet run and not in the Opus run, where the slice finished in about 45 seconds. Right after the first import, a slice that the agent hadn't started sat at 80% for about two minutes.

- Sonnet's three `plate_layout` calls failed with `busy`, "OrcaSlicer does not add a plate while it slices".
- Its `activity_cancel` call failed with `not_found`, "Nothing the tools started has the handle 133". The agent cannot cancel a slice it did not start.
- File › Import was greyed out until I cancelled the slice with the ✕ beside "Slicing…".

I have not checked whether that slice was stuck or only slow, or what started it.

## Note on picking the model

A new project's chat always starts on the provider's default model, Opus 5.5 for Anthropic. The `jusprin_agent.model` setting in the config file doesn't change that default (`AgentHost::default_chat_model` reads the provider profile). The opening message about a newly opened file therefore can't run on any other model.

# The first message after a file is opened or imported

The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.

The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what was loaded and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin, each with bedMm, its bed's width, depth and printable height; selectedPrinterBedMm is the selected printer's. For each object, placedOnBed says whether it sits wholly on the bed now, clear of any area the printer's profile excludes, and fitsSelectedBed and fitsSetupPrinters whether its size fits each bed somewhere, turned a quarter-turn if needed: an object that is off the bed but fits it needs moving, not resizing. mesh is the app's check of the model: shells is how many separate pieces it is made of, openEdges or repairedErrors above zero mean holes or errors in it, and unitsSuspicion says when its size looks like inches or metres. customized lists what the file already prepared for printing: painted supports, seams, colours or fuzzy skin, and its own layer heights. fileFacts is what each 3MF says about itself: the app that saved it, the printer and nozzle it was made for, and its filaments. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain Orca's dialog title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.

Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. When an object does not fit the selected printer, name a set-up printer it fits, from fitsSetupPrinters.

Write a short message, a few sentences, about what matters for this file now:
- Lead with what decides whether or how it can print: a load that failed, an object that does not fit, a printer to choose, settings or G-code that need review. Say it once, with only the numbers that matter.
- Say what you take the object to be, and how it should be printed, only when that changes the advice, and then briefly, as a guess. Leave other advice (material, strength, orientation) until the main decision is made.
- Do not explain routine loading: how the file was opened, whether its settings were applied, or which notices appeared, unless it changes the next step. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.
- When nothing needs attention, say so in a sentence.
- End with one question or offer about the next step, not a menu of alternatives. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved.

Read each actual notice with its automatic answer and the final opening outcome. The guide below is deliberately not a code classification table.

| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
| --- | --- |
| A newer or partly incompatible 3MF asks whether to continue | If opening succeeded, mention a lost or changed feature only when the outcome shows one. If it failed, explain the failure. Omit a version warning with no consequence. |
| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |
| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. G-code is the instructions a printer runs. Name the affected setting if the notice gives it and that helps locate what to review; do not invent a line number or claim I inspected the commands. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |
| A choice to open a 3MF as a project or geometry only | Use loadFacts.settingsOutcome to say whether the file's print settings were applied. Explain only when it changes the next step. |
| Connected-printer synchronization | Use the final selection and separately supplied connection state. Do not infer a connected machine from a preset name. |
| OBJ colour mapping, STEP mesh options, or unreadable STEP names | Mention a resulting colour, shape, precision or naming problem only when it matters to this model. |
| Multiple parts or files become one object | Mention grouping only if it changes how the person can print or edit the model. |
| A suggestion to simplify a very detailed model | Usually omit from the first message unless a current performance or editing problem exists. |
| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |
| “File contains no geometry” or a loading error | Lead with what failed and what, if anything, was added. Give the actual reason when available; do not invent one. |

An alarming notice does not override the final outcome. An automatic “No”, “Yes” or “OK” is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference. If several issues matter, address the most important decision first and briefly flag another consequential issue for later. If selectedSetupChange.printerPreset exists, name both its from and to selections in plain language, then ask which printer the person intends to use. Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item.

Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.

Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short.

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
===== architecture 123-157
### Opening and importing files

Decided 2026-10-24. A file reaches JusPrin in a handful of ways, and they mean one of two things: **start from this file**, or **add this to the project I am working on**. The first is what a person means almost every time they bring a file in; the second is the minority case (a multi-part print), and the person signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent. Because autosave keeps every project, starting a new project by mistake costs one click on Recent, while adding to the wrong project leaves a stray part in it. So every way in starts a new project unless the person aimed at the plate.

| How the file is opened | Model file (STL, STEP, OBJ, AMF, …) | .3mf |
|---|---|---|
| Opened from the OS: a double-click in Finder or Explorer, "Open with", a browser's "open in JusPrin" | New project, named after the file; the app goes to Prepare | New project; the "Previously opened file" question if the file was opened before |
| Dropped on Home | Same | Same |
| Home's **Open…** button, File › Open Project (Cmd+O) | Same | Same |
| Dropped on the Prepare canvas | Added to the open project | New project, as above. OrcaSlicer's "open as project or import geometry?" question is not asked |
| **+ Add model** in the Plates and Project pane, File › Import (Cmd+I) | Added to the open project | Its geometry is added to the open project, without its settings (OrcaSlicer's Import) |
| The Agent composer's + › 3D model, a drop on the Agent pane, or a request in the chat | Attached; the agent adds it to the open project (`object_import`) | Same |

Rules that follow from the table:

- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 a project was always open behind Home (the most recent one resumes at startup).
- A file opened from the OS lands in the running JusPrin. OrcaSlicer's default starts a second process for a .3mf; JusPrin runs as a single instance on every platform.
- Several files opened or dropped together make one new project holding all of them.
- Opening a .3mf as a project is the only thing a .3mf does on the Prepare canvas. Wanting only the geometry out of a .3mf is rare, and the agent or File › Import can do it on request. The one question JusPrin asks on a file open stays the "Previously opened file" question described in the [autosave document](autosave-version-history.md).
- Home's primary action is **Open…**, not Import: there is nothing on Home to import into. The whole Home page accepts a dropped file, and its empty state says so ("Drop a model or project here, or Open…"). Beside it, **New** is the design system's compact outlined button (`secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) for a blank project built up part by part, quiet enough not to compete with Open; File › New Project does the same.
- G-code files keep OrcaSlicer's behavior (the G-code viewer) for now.

**Finding the way to add a part.** With Home's button named Open, the person who wants a second part in the project they have needs to find it from Prepare. Every slicer solves this the same way, with a control inside the workspace that is always on screen: PrusaSlicer's Add button on the top toolbar and Cmd+I, Cura's folder icon at the top left of Prepare, and OrcaSlicer's own Add button on the main toolbar, which JusPrin hides. Dragging onto the plate is in addition to that control in all three, never the only way. JusPrin keeps the same shape: a **+ Add model** button under the plate list in the Plates tab of the Plates and Project pane, drawn like **+ Add plate** and placed directly above it, so the two things that can be added there sit together with the commoner one first (chosen on 2026-10-24 from a drawn comparison against a plus in the tab header and a row under the open plate), plus File › Import (Cmd+I), the composer's + menu, and the empty plate's hint ("Drop a model here or add one"). A person who asks the agent to add a file gets it added as well.

Ownership: the policy is fork-owned (the Home backend, the shell's file handler and the Prepare canvas's drop target, the Plates pane's button). OrcaSlicer keeps its file dialogs, its loading code and its "Previously opened file" seam; the fork adds one seam, `Plater::set_external_file_open_handler`, that lets it take the files handed to `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` (the OS, another instance, the command line, a download, a drop) before OrcaSlicer adds them to the open project, and sets two of OrcaSlicer's own settings (`single_instance`, `project_load_behaviour`) to the values the table needs.

How the paths come out of that one seam:

- The shell's handler (`ShellController::take_opened_files`) leaves a .3mf to OrcaSlicer, which opens it as a project through `load_project` and so asks the "Previously opened file" question; files given with it are added to that project. Any other files are opened in a new project named after the first one: the open project is saved and released the way the agent's `project_open` releases it, then OrcaSlicer's own load runs into the new project, and the app goes to Prepare.
- A drop on the Prepare canvas must add, so the shell replaces OrcaSlicer's `PlaterDropTarget` with its own, which loads through the same call while telling the handler to stand aside. OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own target after every slice; the shell puts its own back on the next idle turn. OrcaSlicer's one-SVG emboss on drop is not kept (the shell hides that gizmo); a dropped SVG loads as an object.
- File › Import › Import Zip Archive also reaches `load_files(wxArrayString)`, so a zip on its own keeps OrcaSlicer's behavior and adds. Home's Open… and a drop on Home open a zip in a new project like any model file.
- A file dropped on Home reaches the app as its name and bytes, not its path: the web view takes the drop. On macOS a native drop target on the web view would not see it: wxWidgets 3.3 gives its WebKit view none of the drag methods it gives its own views, so WebKit's own handling runs (read from the wxWidgets source on 2026-10-24; not yet tried with a real drag). The bytes are written to `JusPrin-dropped/<MD5>/<name>` under the system temp folder and opened from there, so the "Previously opened file" question recognizes a .3mf dropped on Home before, but not one first opened from its own folder.
- The agent's tools load through the vector overload of `load_files` and `load_project`, which the seam does not see, and the handler stands aside while a tool's load runs.

# JusPrin design system

**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.

The original JusPrin logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints were verified from the source SVG. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.

## Brand behavior

- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.

The logo suggests an end-to-end journey through its orbit, precision and momentum through the crossing diagonals, flexible control through the open circle, and technical confidence softened by warmth through the purple gradient.

Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

## Brand palette

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |

The signature gradient runs from Orbit to Bloom. Reserve it for the original logo, splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments. Do not use it as ordinary product chrome.

Product code must resolve colors through semantic tokens in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; raw palette values are not a component API.

## Semantic color behavior

Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.

Core mappings include:

| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `surface.canvas` | `#FFFFFF` | `#17131F` | Main application background |
| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |
| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2B2336` | Dialogs, menus, elevated panels |
| `surface.raisedHover` | `#F6F2F7` | `#3B3047` | The hovered or keyboard-focused row in a menu or popover |
| `text.primary` | `#17131F` | `#F6F2F7` | Headings, values, body copy |
| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |

The JSON token file is authoritative for the code and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values. Every colour it shares with the design system holds the design system's value; `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` pins each one beside its design-system name. Secondary and danger buttons have no colours of their own: like the design system's Button/Secondary they have no fill, a `border.subtle` (secondary) or `status.danger` (danger) stroke, and `text.primary` or `status.danger` text, with `surface.subtle` on hover and `surface.selected` when pressed. `overlay.scrim` and `status.successOnAction` exist only in the code until the Design System artifact adds them.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |

The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
text around it is.

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP, plus a 2 DIP half step (`dimension.space["0.5"]`) used only for the gap between a row's main line and the detail line under it, as in a report finding or a canvas caption.
- The radius scale carries the design system's names (`dimension.radius`):
  - `small`, 4 DIP: standard controls (secondary and icon buttons, fields, the segmented control), matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
  - `medium`, 8 DIP: containers (cards, popovers, chat bubbles) and the primary button, the one branded action.
  - `large`, 12 DIP: sheets, large dialogs and window actions.
  - `chip`, 4 DIP: the printer and filament chip in the header.
  - `full`, 14 DIP: capsule ends of anything up to 28 DIP tall: reply choices, status chips and progress tracks. A shorter box keeps a full capsule, because a radius larger than half the height is drawn as half of it.
- Menus follow the design system's Menu/Popover and Menu/Row: the popover has 8 DIP
  vertical padding, a 1 DIP border and 2 DIP between rows; rows are 36 DIP
  high, run the popover's full width inside its border, and carry no radius,
  so a hovered row is a `surface.raisedHover` band across the panel (lighter
  than the menu in dark mode, never sunk into it). A row has no focus state of
  its own: the keyboard's row is drawn as the hovered one, never with the
  outside focus ring, which would stick out past the popover's edge.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in the design artifacts, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate, warning, and info glyphs sit inside a row of Label or Metadata text, 14 to 16 DIP tall, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. The card's disclosure chevron is an ordinary 16 DIP icon. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- Agent message box: one box with the `medium` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke, and `component.composer` insets (8 DIP padding, 4 DIP between staged files, the field, and the toolbar). The field is Body Small with a 4 DIP inset; it grows a line at a time up to `component.composer.maxLines` (8) and then scrolls, while the toolbar stays visible: the 32 DIP + icon button (or Photo) on the left, Send (`button.primarySmall`, 28 DIP) or Stop (`button.secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) on the right. While the field has the focus the whole box carries the 2 DIP `border.focus` ring. In the app, each + menu choice opens the operating system's file dialog through the host, filtered to that kind. After + come the model and thinking pickers (`button.picker`: 24 DIP, Label, a chevron), which open upward menus no narrower than `component.popover.width`: the model menu lists each set-up provider's models under the provider's name when there is more than one (a provider is added from the Agent settings); the thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model accepts and is left out when it accepts none. A choice belongs to the chat and applies from its next turn. When the full labels do not fit beside + and Send (the composer measures them, so this follows the labels, not a breakpoint), the thinking picker drops "Thinking:" and shows the level alone; if that still does not fit, the model's name is cut with an ellipsis. Both keep their full name as the accessible name and the tooltip. A model menu of more than 12 models opens with the focus in a Field/Search (`component.fieldSearch`: 38 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that becomes 2 DIP `border.strong` with the focus) inset 8 DIP from the menu's sides; the menu is then `component.popover.width` wide and its rows scroll under the field. Typing filters on the model or provider name, ignoring case, the first match carries the menu-row hover fill, Up and Down move it, Enter picks it, and Escape clears the field before it closes the menu. A provider with more than 12 models shows its count beside its name while nothing is typed.
- All settings panel (the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", the four "All settings" boards): opened from the setup card's "All settings" link, it takes the Agent pane's place under a header of the compact icon button back to the chat, the title in Body Bold and the pane's own toggle. A "Showing" row holds the design system's Select (`component.select`: 26 DIP, `small` radius, Body text, a 16 DIP chevron, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that strengthens on hover and becomes the focus ring when open; its menu is the Menu/Popover under its left edge, as wide as the field) listing the whole project, each plate when there are two or more, and each object; it follows the selection in the 3D view. Under it a Field/Search ("Search settings") beside an All / Changed Segmented Control. The presets in use sit in a `surface.subtle` box with the `medium` radius, each filament slot with its Swatch (`component.swatch`, 24 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke). Groups are OrcaSlicer's own pages (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial, Others, then Filament and Printer) with a 32 DIP header row (16 DIP chevron, Body Small Bold name, Label summary at the right) and rows indented 24 DIP: Body Small name and value on a 28 DIP line, a changed value in Body Small Bold with "Preset: …" in Metadata under it. Two or three filament slots stand side by side, one column per slot; more than three go through a slot picker, one at a time. The host reads the whole table in one message (`settings_catalog`, the `all_settings` capability). Only one object's view has anything to press: a Button/Link at the end of a row's note, under the value, where the table marks one — "Use project value" under a setting the object, a part, a modifier or a height range sets itself (not a range's own layer height or filament, which define it), and "Remove" under its support blockers or enforcers. Each press is one OrcaSlicer undo step of the person's, named for what it did, and the panel redraws from the host's next table (`settings_action`, the `settings_actions` capability).
- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 32×32 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius (`component.button.icon`).
- Compact icon target: 26×26 DIP (`component.button.iconCompact`), only for the canvas tool strip and the reset button in a form row, which stands at the field's height.
- Link button: 26 DIP high, 4 DIP horizontal padding, Label Bold in `action.primary`, underlined on hover (`component.button.link`).
- Segmented control: a 30 DIP `surface.subtle` track with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` border and 2 DIP padding, holding 24 DIP segments in Label; the chosen one is `action.primary` (`component.segmented`).
- Tooltip: 24 DIP high, 4×8 DIP padding, Metadata, inverse (`text.primary` fill, `surface.canvas` text) with the subtle elevation (`component.tooltip`). Native tooltips are the operating system's own.
- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`).
- Reply choice (Chat/Reply Choice): drawn as a reply the person could send, not as an app control. 28 DIP high with `component.replyChip` padding, the `full` radius (the one capsule control), Body Small `text.primary` on `surface.subtle` (the person's own bubble) with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke; hover and pressed go to `surface.selected`, never `action.primary`. A tapped choice is sent as the person's bubble in the same tint and words.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the boards on the canvas's Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: an icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude
   artifacts are the source of truth (Kenneth, 2026-10-20; Figma is
   retired): the Design System
   (https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL) and the "JusPrin v2"
   canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). Change the
   token file to match, or, when the code's value is the one to keep, change
   the artifact first. Do not trust old commit messages about either.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

## Runtime application in the native app

The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.

1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
     fonts.
   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
     translucent rounded rectangles.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
     switches at once.
   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
     color.
   - `ColorRGB::orca_accent()` replaces OrcaSlicer's own accent, the teal
     behind `ColorRGB::ORCA()`, `ColorRGBA::ORCA()`, `ImGuiWrapper::COL_ORCA`
     and the preview sliders' `BRAND_COLOR`, with the action color. That
     recolours the ImGui and GL layer: the preview sliders' handles, filled
     track and value text, gizmo highlights, the selection rectangle. Every
     reader evaluates it at use; ImGui's style table, filled once at start-up,
     is filled again through `ImGuiWrapper::reset_style`. The sliders' greys,
     value boxes and handle shape, the legend and the bed stay OrcaSlicer's.
   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`

     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings

contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in

teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is

links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
were not visually verified.

## Design handoff requirements

Every high-fidelity product frame must:

1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
   rather than duplicating every application screen.
2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
3. Use DIP, native density, and the design system's radius scale.
4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (the design system's `code` style uses the system monospace font).
5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.

The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.

**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.

**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.

**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader and skill_read, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too; project_open by the model interrupts the turn, collects the load report with the existing collector and hands it to the new chat through the file-note path; the skill text adds the preset check and asks whether the AI should look at the model instead of attaching a picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".

**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." The plan and disposition table live in the untracked `core-prompt-critique.md` ("Restructure plan", 2026-10-17), as a proposal: Kenneth wants plans presented and decided, not assumed. On 2026-10-17 he had my fast-forward merge of the state-guidance branch undone for that reason (reset, never revert: a revert would litter the log). Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.

**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.

**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.

**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.

**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader and skill_read, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too; project_open by the model interrupts the turn, collects the load report with the existing collector and hands it to the new chat through the file-note path; the skill text adds the preset check and asks whether the AI should look at the model instead of attaching a picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".

**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." The plan and disposition table live in the untracked `core-prompt-critique.md` ("Restructure plan", 2026-10-17), as a proposal: Kenneth wants plans presented and decided, not assumed. On 2026-10-17 he had my fast-forward merge of the state-guidance branch undone for that reason (reset, never revert: a revert would litter the log). Related: [[rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs]], [[project-prompt-sections]], [[tool-call-approval-removed]].

223	Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.
224	
225	**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.
226	
227	**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.
228	
229	**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.

## 2.3 Print intent

This surface answers: **What outcome does the user want?**

Instead of beginning with hundreds of process parameters, the product should ask for meaningful requirements.

### What should remain

- Intended use
- Visual versus functional priority
- Strength direction
- Accuracy requirements
- Important dimensions or clearances
- Heat, chemical, outdoor, food-contact, or flexibility requirements
- Desired surface quality
- Maximum acceptable print time
- Material or color requirements
- Acceptable and unacceptable support contact
- Whether this is a prototype or final part

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

The same model can legitimately be printed with different orientations, materials, wall structures, infill, supports, and tolerances depending on its purpose.

A decorative prototype and a load-bearing final component may use identical geometry but require completely different plans.

### What the agent should do

Translate intent into technical settings. For example:

> “This is a visible decorative object, so I oriented it to protect the front surface, moved the seam to the rear, and accepted a longer print to reduce visible layer artifacts.”

The user should judge that reasoning without having to configure every underlying value.

The full intent editor should appear during project creation, import, or when requirements are incomplete. Afterward, Prepare should retain only a compact editable summary. Specialized questions such as food contact, flexibility, critical clearances, and protected support surfaces should appear contextually rather than in every project.

---

## 2.4 Objects, parts, and plates
----- intent summary lines 150-180
### Default Project-window composition

The default window should contain:

- Project name and saved/unsaved state
- Compact printer pointer: target printer, nozzle, build plate, and material
- Compact, editable intent summary
- Compact active plate/object summary
- 3D Prepare canvas
- Essential direct-manipulation tools
- Compact pinned agent plan
- Highest unresolved assumption, compromise, or risk
- Check print
- Print
- Consequential warnings when applicable

The canvas is the primary human-agent collaboration surface. It must make the build plate and model visible, support camera rotation, pan, zoom, selection, and direct spatial manipulation, and show the changes the agent makes.

The compact summaries should keep the governing assumptions visible without expanding full editors. Examples:

> Decorative · appearance first · protect front surface · under 5 hours

> Plate 1 · Fuzzy Heart · 1 copy · PLA Matte

A one-object project should not permanently display a large object tree. A complete intent questionnaire should not remain expanded after it has been answered.

### Direct resolution of uncertainty

Warnings should link to the user action that resolves them rather than expecting the user to translate them into legacy slicer controls:

- `Support enters this hole` -> `Protect this opening`
