# Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26. A design brainstorm for Kenneth, written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and from the code and design boards named below. No code was changed.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

The setup card is the box pinned at the top of the Agent pane. Its title is meant to be what the print is for, in the person's words, and its headline is the agent's one-line printing plan. Three things go wrong around it.

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The agent may record a title and a plan only through one tool, `setup_record`, and that tool's description says to record only a purpose the person stated and to include one in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, "setup_record"). So before the person says what the print is for, the card's title is the process preset name ("0.20mm Standard @BBL A1") and there is no headline, even after the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody ever states a purpose, like Kenneth's chat of 2026-10-21, stays like that for good.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The purpose and plan belong to the chat and nothing updates them when a model is imported. The app does mark the plan as needing another look (`ProjectPersistence::on_edit` calls `mark_plan_needs_reassessment` for every edit that is not the agent's own, with the import's label as the reason), but that mark goes only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`, `plan.validity`). The card is sent only the title and the headline (`card_context` in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp`), so after the bed-level sheet was imported it still read "Halloween headband costume for my kid · P1S PLA, sturdier walls…" with the state "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there comes from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming the plan.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the first message reads as if the agent spoke unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** When a file opens, the host appends a note message holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`). The page draws that note as nothing whenever the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import does get a visible row, "Import Object: <file> · you · 05:18", but only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves no row. The opening message then describes the moment of loading ("I opened the file, and it switched your setup… Which printer will you print this on?") directly under a card that already shows the printer chosen, the purpose stated and the plan made (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

A fourth, small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis (`.current-setup-title`), so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

The design boards already point part of the way. The product definition asks for a "compact, editable intent summary" whose governing assumptions stay visible, and says the intent editor belongs at project creation and import (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, 2.3 and "Default Project-window composition"). The onboarding board "12 · Prepare intent" on the JusPrin v2 canvas draws that summary with an explicit empty state: "Intent · Not set · not submitted · Add a goal here or discuss it with the Agent". The card's own "Stress · No title" board, on the other hand, falls back to the preset name, which is what the code does. The design system has a Chat/System Line component, "a quiet one-line record of settings, plate tools, answered approvals, or background agent work", with a "you · 15:03" meta on the right.

## Question 1: the title and headline before a purpose is stated

**Option A, keep the preset name.** Status quo. It is honest about the presets but says nothing about the print, reads as a technical label, and the person has no idea the card is waiting for anything from them.

**Option B, the project's name, with a visible "purpose not set" line.** Every project is named after its file (`architecture.md`, "Opening and importing files"), and the name is already in the card's context as `projectName`. The title would read "find_my_hollow" or "petg-pla+support+interface", the presets line stays as it is, and where the headline will go there is one secondary line: "What is this print for? Tell the agent and it will plan around it." That line disappears the moment a purpose is recorded. The empty state is then the same thing the onboarding board draws, and the card never pretends to know the purpose. The cost is that a file name can be ugly, and the line is one more thing on a card the design wants compact.

**Option C, the file's own title when the 3MF carries one.** The load report has `details.title` from the 3MF ("Follow Me Arrow Headband – Festival headband"), which is the author's word for the object, not the model's guess and not a purpose. It reads far better than the file name. The cost is two sources for one slot: STL and STEP files have no title, so the card would say "Follow Me Arrow Headband" for one project and "AMS_disconnect_tool_raised_letters" for the next, and a 3MF title can be marketing copy.

**Recommendation: B, with C as a refinement if Kenneth wants it.** The project name is the one name the Plates and Project pane, Recent and the window already use, so the card agrees with the rest of the app. The headline slot stays empty until the agent records a plan (Question 2); the "purpose not set" line is what fills the gap, and it tells the person the one thing they can do that changes the card.

## Question 2: should recording a plan require a stated purpose?

**Option A, keep the requirement.** Purpose required and stated, or nothing is recorded. The rule exists because the two records drifted when they were separate tools (memory of 2026-10-20). The evidence from both runs is that it starves the card: after the printer and two filaments were confirmed, and a risky machine script found, the card still showed a preset name and no plan.

**Option B, make the purpose optional; keep "stated only".** The plan (headline, decisions, unverified, risks) can be recorded at any time; the purpose may be left out, and when it is, the one already recorded is kept. The rule that a purpose is never inferred stays exactly as written. The headline's rule gains one clause: it says how the print will be made, never what it is for. One tool still writes both records, so they cannot drift apart the way two tools let them. The risk is a weak model writing the inferred purpose into the headline anyway ("Festival headband in PLA…"); that is a prompt-eval case, not a reason to keep the card empty.

**Option C, allow a provisional purpose the agent infers from the file, marked as inferred.** The agent would record "Festival headband (from the file)" and the card would show it with that marker until the person states theirs. This is what a human assistant does out loud ("looks like a festival headband; is that what it's for?"), but it puts a guess in the slot Kenneth reserved for the person's words, and a person who never corrects it ends up with a plan built on a guess.

**Recommendation: B.** The purpose stays the person's. The plan is the agent's, and the agent has one whenever it has decided anything, which is usually well before the purpose is known (which printer, which of the file's two filaments, whether to keep the file's machine scripts). Record it, and the card shows the state of the agent's thinking from the second message on.

## Question 3: when the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan

**Option A, show the app's own mark on the card and make the agent settle it.** The host already knows the plan needs another look and why ("Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl"). Send `planValidity` and `planInvalidatedBy` to the card with the headline. The card then takes the pattern the "Setup card · Out of date" board already draws for estimates: the state label reads "Needs another look" instead of "Confirmed" or "Current", the headline is kept but drawn in the secondary text colour, and under the divider a warning row says "Plan made before: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl was imported". The agent's reply after the import must then either record a new plan or restate the one that still holds, which clears the mark; the file-loaded skill gets that sentence. The purpose stays, because it is the person's statement and adding a part does not change what they said. The cost is a state the model can leave unsettled; the card then says so instead of saying "Confirmed", which is the point.

**Option B, clear the plan on every import.** The card falls back to the purpose with no headline and "No plan for the new contents yet". Simple and never stale, but it throws away a plan that often still holds (a 20 mm tool added beside the headband does not change the headband's strategy), and the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo, so the plan would vanish on a colour change.

**Option C, treat the purpose as stale too.** Mark the purpose when an object is added or removed and ask the person to restate it. Over-engineered: the purpose was about the headband and still is; the agent's job is to ask whether the new object is part of the same print, which Sonnet did in words.

**Recommendation: A.** The app is already right about the plan's state; the card should say what the app knows, and the agent should be the one to clear it. The state-label order becomes: working, then needs another look, then updated, then the existing states. "Confirmed" should never show while the plan carries the mark.

## Question 4: showing the event that started the chat

**Option A, draw the file-load note as a Chat/System Line.** The note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf` makes it the anchor and the agent's message its reply), it just draws as nothing. Draw it as the design system's system line: "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 05:16", or for an import "Added Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl · you · 05:20". The agent's message then reads as what it is, a dated reaction to that row, and the card above reads as now. An import already has a change row saying the same thing ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18"), so one of the two must go: keep the change row, which carries the revert affordance, and draw the note's line only when the load created the project. When the Agent could not speak, the note already draws as the "Notes about this file" card; that stays.

**Option B, a bubble in the person's voice ("I opened find_my_hollow.3mf").** Rejected: bubbles are words someone wrote, and the person wrote none.

**Option C, keep the note hidden and have the message name its trigger in words.** "You opened find_my_hollow.3mf, and it switched…". Cheapest, but it depends on the model every time, says nothing about when, and does nothing for the staleness under the card.

**Recommendation: A.** A dated row is also the honest answer to "the opening message goes stale": a message under "Opened … · 05:16" is visibly history once the card says something else, the same way the design's timeline treats an agent response as the answer to the turn above it. The reply choices under the opening message already close once answered, so the question does not stay clickable.

## Question 5: how long the opening message should be, and what it leaves to the card

Today's opening messages ran to about 230 words (Opus, four bullets and a question) and about 150 (Sonnet's import). Both repeated what the card shows (the preset switch, the two filaments) and the Opus one stated something wrong about the PLA that it had to correct in the next turn; length invites that. The skill already asks for "a few sentences".

**Option A, one decision and one question, under about 80 words.** Lead with the thing that decides whether or how the print can go ahead (which printer, a part that does not fit, a modified machine script), at most one secondary flag, then the one question. Presets, plate, estimates and object count are the card's and are not repeated. What was checked is the turn line's ("Worked for 9s · 3 actions", which opens into the list). The file author's advice waits until the gating decision is made, as the skill already says.

**Option B, the current shape.** Everything found, as bullets. It is the most-read message in the product and it sets the tone, but it goes stale fastest and overlaps the card most.

**Option C, a bare question when nothing blocks.** "Nothing needs attention. Which printer will you print this on?" and nothing else. Right for a clean STL on a known printer; too thin when the file switched the printer and carries two materials.

**Recommendation: A, with C as its lower bound.** The cap is a prompt-eval check (word count, bullet count, exactly one question), and the skill's "Write a short message" line becomes concrete numbers so it can be measured.

## Sketches

Panel at its narrow width. The card is on `surface.subtle`; rows under it are system lines in the secondary colour.

### A model file opened as a new project, before anyone has spoken

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                      Not sliced │
│ petg-pla+support+interface                    │   ← project name (Q1, option B)
│ 0.20mm Standard · Generic PETG +1             │
│ What is this print for? Tell the agent and    │   ← shown until a purpose is recorded
│ it will plan around it.                       │
│ Not sliced yet · estimates unavailable        │
│ Compute estimates                             │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ All settings                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Opened petg-pla+support+interface.3mf as a    │   ← Chat/System Line (Q4, option A)
│ new project                        you · 12:31│
│                                               │
│ This file was made for the Bambu Lab A1 and   │   ← ≤ 80 words, one question (Q5)
│ switched your printer to it. The headband is  │
│ 254 × 252 mm, so of your printers only the A1 │
│ and the Qidi X-Plus 4 can hold it. It also    │
│ uses PETG with a PLA separating layer, which  │
│ needs a filament changer. Which printer will  │
│ you print this on?                            │
│ (Bambu Lab A1) (Qidi X-Plus 4) (Anycubic K…)  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

# Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26, revised the same day after Kenneth's feedback: start from why the card exists, and prefer the shape that is too simple to have problems over the one with no obvious problems. Written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and the code and design boards listed at the end. No code was changed.

## Why the card exists

The person is talking to an agent that changes their project. The project's real state lives in OrcaSlicer, not in any message, and messages go stale the moment the next turn happens. The chat is a log; the All settings panel is an editor; the card is the one place in the Agent pane that is always *now*. It answers, without scrolling and without reading: what is this print being made with right now, what is the agent working toward, and what will it cost. The product definition asks for exactly that set on the default window: a compact printer pointer, a compact editable intent summary, a compact pinned agent plan, and the highest unresolved risk (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, "Default Project-window composition" and 2.3 "Print intent").

Two things follow from that purpose, and they decide every question below.

First, **everything on the card must be something the app can know is true now.** Presets, plate, estimates and object counts come from OrcaSlicer and are true by construction. The purpose and the plan are text the agent wrote, and the card can only show them honestly if the app tracks whether the project has moved on since they were written. For the plan it already does (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment` on every edit that is not the agent's own). For the purpose it does not need to: those are the person's words and change only when the person changes them.

Second, **anything that is a record of a moment belongs in the timeline, not on the card.** "Updated" for one minute after the agent's change, the last project step with its Undo, the estimate before and after, "You set Wall loops 3 outside the agent. Your current settings are preserved.", "Confirmed": these are all notes about something that just happened. The timeline already draws every change as a row with who and when and a revert point (`ChangeRows.tsx`). The card drawing them too is why it has twelve named states today (`setupPresentation` in `SetupCard.tsx`: Preset fallback, No agent, Agent working, Updated, Confirmed, Edited by you, Out of date, Not sliced, Current, Earlier setup, Saved sliced snapshot, Sliced & sent), and why each fix for one of them has opened a hole for the next.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The one tool that writes the card's title and plan, `setup_record`, requires a stated purpose in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`). So after a file opens, the title is the process preset name and there is no headline, even once the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody states a purpose, like Kenneth's of 2026-10-21, stays that way.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The app marks the plan as needing another look after an import, with the import's label as the reason, but sends the mark only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`); the card gets the title and headline alone (`card_context` in `AgentHost.cpp`). So after the bed-level sheet was imported the card still read the headband plan and said "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there came from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming anything.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the opening message reads as unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** The host appends a note holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`); the page draws that note as nothing when the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import gets a visible row only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves none. The message then describes the moment of loading under a card that shows a later state (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

And a small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis, so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

## The simple card

Six slots, each with one source and one empty form. No state machine; the only thing on the right of the eyebrow is "Agent working" while a turn runs, because that is the one card-wide "now" fact.

```
Setup summary                        [Agent working]
<purpose the person stated · else the project's name>
<process · first filament (+n)>
<plan headline · else nothing>
  ↳ when the app has marked the plan: "Plan needs another look · <reason>"
<estimates · "Not sliced yet" · "Recomputing…" · "Previous estimates · not current">
<warning rows from the app's own checks, e.g. printer reports PLA, setup uses PETG>
All settings
```

The rule for the two agent-written slots is the same rule the estimates slot already has: a record the app knows is behind the project is shown with "not current" beside it, never silently kept and never silently deleted. The estimates do this today ("Previous estimates · not current" on the "Setup card · Out of date" board); the plan gets the identical treatment.

What leaves the card, and where it already lives:

| Leaves the card | Already lives in |
|---|---|
| "Updated" for a minute, the last step, Undo, estimate before → after | the change rows under the turn, with "Revert to here" |
| "Edited by you outside the agent" note | the person's change row, plus "Plan needs another look · Wall loops 2 → 3" on the card |
| "Confirmed" | nothing; it was the recompute state wearing the wrong word |
| The separate "Preset fallback" and "No agent" renderings | the same six slots; with no agent the plan slot reads "No agent configured" |

The saved card of an earlier chat (historical, "Saved with this chat") is a different object, a snapshot, and is not changed by this note.

The cost of the cut is one click: Undo of the agent's last project step was on the card; it becomes the timeline row's revert, which is one scroll away at most because the row sits under the turn that made it. I think that is the right trade; the card should not carry an action whose meaning changes a minute later.

## The five questions under that shape

**1. Title and headline before a purpose is stated.** The title slot shows the purpose or, when there is none, the project's name, which is the file's name (`architecture.md`, "Opening and importing files") and is already in the card's context as `projectName`. Nothing else: no "purpose not set" hint line, no preset name. Asking for the purpose is the agent's job in its message, where it already is. The headline slot is empty until the agent records a plan.

The earlier draft of this note proposed a hint line and, as a refinement, the 3MF's own title. Both are extra states for the no-purpose case; the project name is one rule that is true in every case and matches how the Plates and Project pane and Recent name the same thing.

**2. Should recording a plan require a stated purpose?** No. The purpose becomes optional in `setup_record`; when it is left out, the recorded one is kept. The rule that a purpose is never inferred stays as written, and the headline's rule gains one clause: it says how the print will be made, never what it is for. This removes a coupling rather than adding anything. Both records still come through one tool, so they cannot drift apart the way the two old tools let them. The evidence for the change is both runs: the agent had chosen a printer and two filaments and found a risky machine script, and the card showed none of it.

**3. When the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan.** Send the plan's validity and reason to the card beside the headline. The headline line reads "Plan needs another look · imported Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl" until the agent either records a new plan or restates the one that holds, both of which clear the mark; the file-loaded skill tells it to do one or the other in the same reply. The purpose is untouched: adding a part does not change what the person said the print is for. Nothing is cleared automatically, because the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo, and a plan that vanished on a colour change would be a worse surprise than one that says it needs a look.

**4. Showing the event that started the chat.** Every event that starts a turn gets a row; the hidden note is the one exception today and it goes. The file-load note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf`); draw it as the design system's Chat/System Line, "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 12:16", when the load created the project. An import already has its change row ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18"), which carries the revert point, so the note draws nothing there and the change row stays the trigger. The agent's message is then a dated reply to a dated row, and the card above is now. That is the whole answer to "the opening message goes stale": it is history, drawn as history, like every other turn in the design's timeline. The reply choices under it already close once answered.

**5. How long the opening message should be.** About 80 words, at most two bullets, exactly one question, measured by the prompt evals. It leads with the decision that gates printing (which printer, a part that does not fit, a modified machine script), and leaves presets, plate and estimates to the card and the list of checks to the turn line ("Worked for 9s · 3 actions"). Today's messages ran to about 230 words (Opus) and 150 (Sonnet), repeated the card, and the long one stated something wrong that the next turn had to correct.

## Sketches

## The alternative I considered and set aside

Drop the purpose and plan from the card altogether and show only OrcaSlicer facts: project name, presets, estimates, warnings, All settings. That card can never be wrong, and it needs no staleness rule at all. I set it aside because it would no longer answer "what is the agent working toward", which is half of why the card exists, and because the product definition puts the intent summary and the pinned plan on the default window. If Kenneth would rather have the card that cannot lie than the card that says when it might, this is the shape, and it is simpler still.

- The slice that sat at 80% during the Sonnet run, out of scope as the task said.

1. **Should the card be cut to the six slots above, with the moment-of-change notes (Updated, last step with Undo, estimate delta, edited-by-you) left to the timeline rows?** The alternative keeps today's card and fixes the three faults inside it. I recommend the cut; it is the change that makes the other five small.

2. **Before a purpose is stated, should the title be the project's name, with no hint line?** The alternatives are the preset name (today) or a hint line inviting the purpose. I recommend the project name alone.

3. **May the agent record a plan before the person has stated a purpose, with the purpose still never inferred?** No keeps the card empty for every chat that starts from a file. I recommend yes.

8. **Or, instead of 1 to 4: should the card show only OrcaSlicer facts and no agent-written text at all?** Simplest of all and never wrong; it gives up the pinned purpose and plan. I lean against, for the reason above, but it is the honest other end of the simplicity scale.

# Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26, revised twice the same day after Kenneth's feedback: start from why the card exists, keep it simple, and give the card one mental model (agent's words above a line, facts below it). Written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and the code and design boards listed at the end. No code was changed.

## Why the card exists

The person is talking to an agent that changes their project. The project's real state lives in OrcaSlicer, not in any message, and messages go stale the moment the next turn happens. The chat is a log; the All settings panel is an editor; the card is the one place in the Agent pane that is always *now*. It answers, without scrolling and without reading: what is this print for and how does the agent mean to make it, and what is actually in force. The product definition asks for exactly that on the default window: a compact intent summary, a compact pinned agent plan, a compact printer pointer, and the highest unresolved risk (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, "Default Project-window composition" and 2.3 "Print intent").

Three rules follow, and they decide every question below.

1. **Everything on the card must be something the app can know is true now.** Presets, estimates and counts come from OrcaSlicer and are true by construction. The plan is agent text, and the app already tracks whether the project has moved on since it was written (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment` runs on every edit that is not the agent's own). The purpose is the person's words and changes only when they change it.

2. **A record of a moment belongs in the timeline, not on the card.** "Updated" for a minute, the last step with Undo, the estimate before and after, the "edited by you outside the agent" note, "Confirmed": these are notes about something that just happened. The change rows already draw each of them with who, when and a revert point (`ChangeRows.tsx`). Drawing them on the card too is why it has twelve named states today (`setupPresentation` in `SetupCard.tsx`) and why each fix for one opened a hole for the next.

3. **The card never warns about anything it does not itself state.** A warning on the card is an annotation of the line it contradicts, one per line, in the status colour. A warning with no line to attach to is not the card's; it belongs to the canvas, the print-issues chip or the chat, which already show it. This is what keeps the warnings from growing again: a new one has to name the card line it is about, or it is refused.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The one tool that writes the card's title and plan, `setup_record`, requires a stated purpose in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`). So after a file opens the title is the process preset name and there is no headline, even once the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody states a purpose, like Kenneth's of 2026-10-21, stays that way.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The app marks the plan as needing another look after an import, with the import's label as the reason, but sends the mark only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`); the card gets the title and headline alone (`card_context` in `AgentHost.cpp`). So after the bed-level sheet was imported the card still read the headband plan and said "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there came from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming anything.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the opening message reads as unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** The host appends a note holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`); the page draws that note as nothing when the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import gets a visible row only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves none. The message then describes the moment of loading under a card that shows a later state (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

And a small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis, so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

## The card: words above the line, facts below it

```
Setup summary                              [Agent working]
<the purpose, in the person's words>                       ┐ words: present only when
<the plan's headline, in the agent's words>                │ someone has written them
   ↳ marked by the app: "Plan needs another look · <reason>"┘
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
0.20mm Standard · Generic PETG +1 · 4 settings changed   All settings
   ↳ "Printer last reported PLA" when the device disagrees
◷ ~1h 05m  ⬡ 23 g  ▦ Plate 1  $0.68
   ↳ "Not sliced yet" · "Recomputing…" · "Previous estimates · not current"
```

Above the line is what the person and the agent have said: the purpose and the plan. When neither has said anything yet, the section is absent and the card is the facts under its eyebrow. Nothing stands in for the missing words: not the preset name, not the project name (the window title and the Plates pane already show that), not a hint line. Asking for the purpose is the agent's job in its message, where it already is.

Below the line is what is in force, from OrcaSlicer: the process and filament presets with how many settings differ from them (the card's context already carries `presetDeltas`), the estimates, and the door to all of it. The All settings panel's All/Changed switch is what "4 settings changed" opens onto.

Each fact line has one annotation slot, used only when the app knows that line is not what it appears. The estimates already work this way ("Previous estimates · not current" on the "Setup card · Out of date" board). The plan gets the same treatment, and so does the filament line when the printer reports a different spool. The only thing right of the eyebrow is "Agent working", the one card-wide "now" fact.

What leaves the card, and where it already lives:

| Leaves the card | Already lives in |
|---|---|
| "Updated" for a minute, the last step, Undo, estimate before → after | the change rows under the turn, with "Revert to here" |
| "Edited by you outside the agent" note | the person's change row, and "Plan needs another look · Wall loops 2 → 3" |
| "Confirmed" | nothing; it was the recompute state wearing the wrong word |
| The preset name as a title | nothing; the preset is a fact line |
| The separate "Preset fallback" and "No agent" renderings | the same card; with no agent the words section is absent and a fact line says "No agent configured" |
| Free-standing warning rows | each becomes a line's annotation, or goes to the surface that owns it (below) |

The saved card of an earlier chat ("Saved with this chat") is a snapshot of this card and is not changed by this note.

### Where today's warnings go under rule 3

Today the card has three sources of warnings (`deterministicAttention` and the out-of-date block in `SetupCard.tsx`; nothing else passes it findings):

- **The printer last reported a different material, nozzle, model or plate than the setup uses.** Material annotates the filament line ("Printer last reported PLA"). Nozzle and model are not lines on this card: the printer lives in the header's printer and filament chip (`Shell/PrinterFilamentChip.hpp`), so a nozzle or model mismatch is that chip's to show, and the chat's. Plate type is not a line either; if it matters enough to show, the plate's name on the estimates line is where it attaches ("Plate 1 · printer reports Cool Plate").
- **Estimates no longer match the project.** Already an annotation of the estimates line.
- **A calibration project whose test steps were lost.** In a calibration chat the test is the plan, so it annotates the plan line. It is the one case that needs a home chosen; it is small.

Print issues from the slice (overhangs, thin walls, collisions) are not the card's: the canvas marks them and the chat has its print-issues chip. The card states nothing about the slice's quality, so by rule 3 it cannot warn about it.

The cost of the cut is one click: Undo of the agent's last project step was on the card; it becomes the timeline row's revert, one scroll away under the turn that made it. The card should not carry an action whose meaning changes a minute later.

## The five questions under that shape

**1. Title and headline before a purpose is stated.** Neither. The words section is absent until the person states a purpose or the agent records a plan. The earlier drafts of this note proposed the project name, a hint line, and the 3MF's own title in turn; each was another state for the empty case. The empty case is simply the facts.

**2. Should recording a plan require a stated purpose?** No. The `purpose` argument of `setup_record` becomes optional; left out, the recorded one is kept. The rule that a purpose is never inferred stays as written, and the headline's rule gains one clause: it says how the print will be made, never what it is for. Nothing new is added: no tool, no structure. The agent already decides when it has a strategy worth recording ("call it with a headline before applying several changes for one request, and again whenever the strategy changes"), and in both runs it had one well before the purpose: which printer, which of the file's two filaments, whether to keep the file's machine scripts. The one cost is churn: a model allowed to record earlier may record more often, and the headline may read "waiting on a printer" rather than a strategy. That is a prompt-eval case, not a reason to keep the words section empty. Until the agent records, the section stays absent, which is honest.

**3. When the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan.** Send the plan's validity and reason to the card beside the headline. The plan line reads "Plan needs another look · imported Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl" until the agent either records a new plan or restates the one that holds, both of which clear the mark; the file-loaded skill tells it to do one or the other in the same reply. The purpose is untouched: adding a part does not change what the person said the print is for. Nothing is cleared automatically, because the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo.

**4. Showing the event that started the chat.** Every event that starts a turn gets a row; the hidden note is the one exception today and it goes. The file-load note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf`); draw it as the design system's Chat/System Line, "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 12:16", when the load created the project. An import already has its change row ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18") carrying the revert point, so the note draws nothing there and the change row stays the trigger. The agent's message is then a dated reply to a dated row, and the card above is now. The reply choices under it already close once answered.

**5. How long the opening message should be.** About 80 words, at most two bullets, exactly one question, measured by the prompt evals. It leads with the decision that gates printing and leaves presets, plate and estimates to the card and the list of checks to the turn line. Today's messages ran to about 230 words (Opus) and 150 (Sonnet), repeated the card, and the long one stated something wrong that the next turn had to correct.

## Sketches

Panel at its narrow width. Every string in a card or a row below is from the saved chats in `card-headline-repro/`; the agent's opening messages are shortened to the proposed cap and are the one illustrative text.

### Case (a): a model file opened as a new project, before anyone has spoken

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                                 │
│ 0.20mm Standard · Generic PETG +1             │   ← facts only; nobody has said anything yet
│   All settings                                │
│ Not sliced yet                                │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Opened petg-pla+support+interface.3mf as a    │   ← Chat/System Line
│ new project                        you · 12:31│
│                                               │
│ This file was made for the Bambu Lab A1 and   │   ← ≤ 80 words, one question
│ switched your printer to it. The headband is  │
│ 254 × 252 mm, so of your printers only the A1 │
│ and the Qidi X-Plus 4 can hold it. It also    │
│ uses PETG with a PLA separating layer, which  │
│ needs a filament changer. Which printer will  │
│ you print this on?                            │
│ (Bambu Lab A1) (Qidi X-Plus 4) (Anycubic K…)  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

After the person chooses the A1 the card is unchanged until the agent records a plan; when it does, the plan line appears above the rule. When the person later says "it's part of my kid's Halloween costume", their words appear above the plan. The rows under the card stay dated where they were.

### Case (a) after the purpose, as Opus recorded it

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                                 │
│ Kid's Halloween arrow headband that flexes    │   ← the person's purpose, wrapped
│ without snapping                              │
│ Headband alone in PETG, flat, solid-wall      │   ← the agent's headline
│ band, no supports                             │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ 0.20mm Standard · Generic PETG +1 ·           │
│ 2 settings changed              All settings  │
│ ◷ ~1h 05m  ⬡ 23 g  ▦ Plate 1  $0.68           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Case (b): a model imported into a project whose chat already holds a recorded purpose and plan

This is the Sonnet run: `find_my_hollow.3mf` was opened, the person wrote in the chat that the headband is a Halloween costume for their kid, Sonnet recorded that purpose and its plan with `setup_record`, and then `Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl` was imported. The purpose and plan here are the chat's records, not the 3MF author's description.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                                 │
│ Halloween headband costume for my kid         │   ← the person's words stay
│ P1S PLA, sturdier walls for the clip, arrow   │   ← the plan, kept
│ and tool on separate plates                   │
│   Plan needs another look ·                   │   ← the app's mark, as an annotation
│   imported Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl           │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ 0.20mm Standard · Bambu PLA Basic +2 ·        │
│ 1 setting changed               All settings  │
│ Recomputing…                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ✎ Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl     │   ← the existing change row is the trigger
│                                    you · 05:20│
│                                               │
│ That sheet is a 203 × 203 mm bed-levelling    │
│ test, one layer thick, not part of the        │
│ headband, and it cannot share plate 1 with    │
│ the arrow. Should I put it on its own plate,  │
│ or leave it out of this print?                │
│ (Own plate) (Leave it out)                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The agent's reply re-records or confirms the plan, and the annotation goes.

## The alternative I considered and set aside

Drop the words section altogether and show only OrcaSlicer facts. That card can never be wrong and needs no staleness rule. I set it aside because it would no longer answer "what is the agent working toward", which is half of why the card exists, and because the product definition puts the intent summary and the pinned plan on the default window. It is the honest other end of the simplicity scale, and the facts half of the card above is exactly that card, so choosing it later costs nothing.

## What this does not settle

- The slice that sat at 80% during the Sonnet run, out of scope as the task said.
- Whether a plan recorded before a purpose counts as checked once a purpose is stated. Today a first or changed purpose fires the setup-changed skill, which asks the agent to check the presets; that keeps working, and the agent re-records then.
- Whether the header's printer chip should carry the nozzle and model mismatches the card drops. Rule 3 says they are the chip's; this note does not design the chip.

## Decisions that are Kenneth's

Each changes what the person sees, so none is mine. Each is a question with its alternative and my lean.

1. **Should the card take the two-part shape: the person's purpose and the agent's plan above a rule, the presets with a changed-settings count, estimates and All settings below it, and nothing else?** The alternative keeps today's card and fixes the three faults inside it. I recommend the two-part shape; it is the change that makes the other questions small.

2. **When nobody has stated a purpose or recorded a plan, should the words section be absent, so the card is the facts alone?** The alternatives are the preset name (today), the project name, or a hint line asking for the purpose. I recommend absent.

3. **May the agent record a plan before the person has stated a purpose, with the purpose still never inferred?** No keeps the words section empty for every chat that starts from a file until the person volunteers a purpose. I recommend yes; it changes one argument from required to optional and adds nothing.

4. **Should a warning appear on the card only as an annotation of the fact line it contradicts, so that print issues, nozzle and printer-model mismatches leave the card for the canvas, the chat and the header chip?** The alternative is today's free-standing warning rows, which any check can add to. I recommend the annotation rule.

5. **When the project changes under a plan, should the plan line carry "Plan needs another look · reason" until the agent re-records or confirms, with the purpose untouched and nothing cleared automatically?** The alternative is to clear the plan on such changes. I recommend the annotation.

6. **Should the file that created the project get a dated system line in the chat, with imports keeping their change row?** The alternative is to leave the event invisible and ask the model to name it in words. I recommend the row.

7. **Should the opening message be capped at about 80 words, two bullets and one question?** The alternative is today's bullet list of everything found. I recommend the cap.

8. **Should the purpose wrap to two lines, or should its limit drop to what one line holds (about 45 characters at the narrow width)?** Either removes "sna…". I lean towards two lines, since the person's words are the one thing on the card that should not be cut.

## Sources read

- `card-headline-repro/REPORT.md`, its five screenshots and both saved chats (`repro-project*/current-state.json`).

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (`card_context`, `on_file_loaded`, `continue_after_tool`, the chat-title generator), `ToolRegistry.cpp` (`setup_record`), `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` (the `SetupRecord` handler), `ProjectPersistence.cpp` and `ProjectStateDocument.cpp` (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment`), `ProviderAgent.cpp`; `Shell/PrinterFilamentChip.hpp` for where the printer lives in the header.
- `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `design-system.md`, `architecture.md` ("Opening and importing files"), `product-definition.md` (2.3 "Print intent", "Default Project-window composition").
- The JusPrin v2 canvas: boards "Setup card · Current · Collapsed/Expanded", "Setup card · Out of date", "Stress · No title", "Stress · Long title", "Pinned Setup Card", "Chat/System Line · Light & Dark", "print-timeline-panel-full", "12 · Prepare intent", "message-states · conversation content matrix". content.text:
Answers to the four questions, then what changed in the note.

**"A1 confirmed, file's PETG + PLA kept…": how is it generated?** By the agent, through the existing setup_record tool, as its plan headline. No new tool and no new structure. The only change is that the tool's purpose argument becomes optional instead of required, so the agent may record a plan before the person has said what the print is for. The tool's description already tells it when to record: before applying several changes for one request, and whenever the strategy changes. That particular string was my invention, though, since the agent never got to record before the purpose in either run. I have taken it out of the sketches. Every card string in the note is now from the saved chats, and the empty slot stays empty until the agent writes something.

**"A project that already has a purpose and a plan": the 3MF author's text?** No. It means the chat's own records from the Sonnet run: the person wrote that the headband is a Halloween costume for their kid, Sonnet recorded that purpose and its plan through setup_record, and then the bed-level sheet was imported. The 3MF's author description never reaches the card. The heading and the paragraph under it now say so.

**The presets line is out of place.** Agreed, and your mental model is better than my slot list. The note now draws the card as words above a rule and facts below it. "unfinished work" there.

## What is here

- `published/` — an exact copy of what is published now (`canvas/project`, `ds/project`). Every re-sync is
  compared against it, then it is replaced by the new build.
- `figma/spec3/<page id>.txt` — the Figma pages as last read (one text line per layer). `figma/vars.json` —

- `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` — the published files, the Figma reads and the scripts as they were

- Hover and pressed change the fill, not the size: quiet controls go to `surface-subtle` then `surface-selected`; the primary action goes to `action-primary-hover` then `action-primary-pressed`.
- Fields show state on their stroke: 1px `border-subtle` at rest, `border-strong` on hover, 2px `border-focus` when focused, 1px `status-danger` with a message when wrong, and an `action-disabled` fill when disabled.
- Disabled controls keep their shape. Filled and icon buttons drop to 40% opacity, outlined buttons to 50%; fields, selects and chips switch to `action-disabled` and `action-disabled-text`. Do not hide a disabled action.
- Actions: `ButtonPrimary` once per view, `ButtonSecondary` for other labelled actions, `ButtonIcon` when a glyph alone is unmistakable, `ButtonLink` for low-emphasis moves such as "‹ Back" and "Undo", and `ButtonSplit` when the main action has alternatives.
- Entry: `FieldText`, `FieldSecret` for codes and keys, `FieldSearch` to filter a list, `FieldNumber` for one parameter, `FieldVerificationCode` for a six-digit code. Choice: `SegmentedControl` for two to five short options, `Select` for more, `Checkbox` for on or off, `Swatch` for a filament colour.
- Menus are a `MenuPopover` of `MenuRow`s, grouped with `MenuSectionTitle`. Focused tasks sit in a `Sheet`; an action that cannot be undone asks first with `DialogConfirmation`.
- Canvas tools use a `ToolPanel` of `FormRow`s. Status is shown with `StatusDot` and `Progress`, always beside words. `Stepper` marks position in a short setup sequence; `Tooltip` names icon-only controls; `DisclosureTechnicalDetails` folds away secondary detail.
- The Agent pane is built from `ChatHeader`, `PinnedSetupCard`, `ChatBubble`, `ChatReplyChoice`, `ChatAttachment`, `ChatTurnActivity`, `ChatToolActivity` and `Composer`. The header carries `ChipPrinterSpool`; the Home screen lists `ProjectCard`s and `PrinterCard`s.
- Draw every glyph with `Icon`.

## Accessibility

- Text meets 4.5:1 on the surface its token names; large text, control boundaries that carry meaning, icons and focus rings meet 3:1.
- Keyboard focus is a visible 2px `border-focus` ring, offset 2px. Never signal focus with a fill change alone.
- `status-warning` is the one exception in light mode, at about 2.5:1 on `surface-canvas`: use it for the warning glyph only, beside a `text-primary` label.
- `border-subtle` is decorative. A control must be recognisable by its label or glyph without it.

"""Replaces the old one-row Input block in each screen spec with the new Composer's lines."""
import re, sys
from spec_lines import composer_spec
PH = 'Ask about this print or request a change…'
ind = lambda l: len(l) - len(l.lstrip(' '))
for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    L = open(f).read().split('\n')
    i = next(k for k, l in enumerate(L) if PH in l)
    j = i
    while not (ind(L[j]) < ind(L[i]) and L[j].strip().startswith('Input')): j -= 1
    k = j + 1
    while k < len(L) and ind(L[k]) > ind(L[j]): k += 1
    w = int(re.search(r'\]\s+(\d+)x', L[j]).group(1))

Below the rule: the process and filament presets with the count of settings that differ from them ("5 settings changed", from the context's `presetDeltas` plus object overrides) and the All settings link beside it; then the estimates, or the one line that stands in for them ("Not sliced yet" with Compute estimates, "Time & material estimates recomputing…"). The only card-wide state label is "Agent working". Remove from the card: "Updated" for a minute, the last step with Undo, the estimate before/after, the "edited by you outside the agent" note, "Confirmed", the free-standing warning rows, and the nozzle and printer-model mismatches (the timeline rows and the header's printer chip own those). Its brief names the five decisions, the files for each, the tests and the harness, the build limits for the shared Mac, and the docs it must update in the same commits: the design-system doc's setup-card and All-settings entries, the product definition and architecture docs where they describe the card or the file-load note, both skills, the setup_record description, and the Testing README. It also tells the agent to grep for every description of the old card so none survives. The model and worktree were yours to pick on the card. I'll relay its report when its turn ends.

**On moving PinnedSetupCard out of the design system.** No document states a rule for what belongs in the design system. I checked the agent docs, the design system's own README and the memory notes. The nearest thing is the README's "Components and states" section, which simply lists what is there, and that list already mixes primitives (buttons, fields, menus) with product compositions: the Agent pane's eight components including PinnedSetupCard, ChatTurnActivity and Composer, plus ChipPrinterSpool, ProjectCard and PrinterCard.

Two facts matter for the decision. First, the coded components are a drawing kit, not product code. The app's React page does not import the design system's bundle, and none of the canvas boards mount a coded component either. The coded PinnedSetupCard has exactly one consumer: its own preview card in the design system. Today's 90-board rework drew the card from a Python generator, not from that component. Second, the card changes whenever a product decision changes, as it did today. Every such change is a design-system release plus a copy into the canvas's own design-system folder.

So the question is really "what is the design system for". Two answers are defensible:
- **Vocabulary only.** Tokens, type, and the reusable controls and chat pieces that appear on more than one surface. A one-instance composition such as the setup card lives with its product page, drawn on the canvas as a board family, with its rules in the product docs. Under this rule PinnedSetupCard leaves, and so should PrinterCard, ProjectCard and probably ChatToolActivity, which are the same kind of thing.
- **Everything the app draws from tokens.** Primitives and compositions alike, which is what the README documents today. Under this rule the card stays, and the value is one coded definition that the canvas could mount instead of redrawing, which nobody has done yet.

My recommendation is to write the rule down first, in the design-system doc and the design system's README, and apply it to the whole set at once rather than move one component. I lean towards the vocabulary-only rule, because the card's content is a product decision and the generator that drew it today lives with the canvas tools anyway. Moving only PinnedSetupCard would leave the list inconsistent and the question would come back with the next component.

===== setup-card-two-part-report.md
# Setup card in two parts: report (2026-10-26)

Commit `0e59bd287c` on branch `claude/setup-card-two-part`, cut from `jusprin-newui` at `88a172b3a3`. It is not pushed. It merges cleanly onto the current `jusprin-newui` (`2bb0cb0f1a`, the auto-slice revert). This report is untracked: do not commit it.

## Problem

Kenneth's 2026-10-26 decisions (in `setup-card-opening-message-design-note.md`) reshape four things:
- **The setup card** gets two parts. Above a rule are the words someone wrote. Below it are OrcaSlicer's facts. Warnings appear only as annotations of the line they contradict.
- **The plan's mark** is cleared only when the agent records the plan again.
- **`setup_record`'s purpose** becomes optional.
- **The opening message** gets a cap, and the chat gets a one-line note for a file opened as a new project.

## What was built

- **Card** (`SetupCard.tsx`, `styles.css`):
  - Purpose and headline sit above a rule. They are absent until recorded.
  - Below the rule:
    - the presets line with "N settings changed" (preset deltas plus object overrides), with All settings beside it;
    - then the estimates, or "Not sliced yet" with Compute estimates, or "…recomputing…".
  - Three annotations, each with the 14 px triangle-alert glyph:
    - plan mark;
    - "Printer last reported X";
    - "Previous estimates · not current" with Recompute.
  - The only card-wide state is "Agent working".
  - Saved cards keep their eyebrow, "Saved <date>" and the footnote.
- **Host**: `card_context` sends `planValidity` and `planInvalidatedBy`. The `undo_setup_change` action is removed, because only the card used it.
- **`setup_record`**:
  - A call needs a purpose or a headline.
  - If the purpose is left out, the recorded one is kept and the result says "unchanged".
  - The description now says the headline describes how the print will be made, never what it is for.
  - `project_tools.json` is regenerated.
- **Skills**:
  - Both skills now say: re-record the plan when it needs reassessment.
  - The file-loaded skill caps the opening message at about 80 words, two bullets and exactly one question, and leaves presets, plate and estimates to the card.
- **Chat**: "Opened <file> as a new project · you · <time>" draws in the `message note` style. An import draws nothing.
- **Docs**: design-system.md, product-definition.md, architecture.md (opening files), mcp-tool-extension-guide.md, and the code comments that described the old card.

## Tests and results

- **Vitest**: 611 passing (including `wording.test.ts` and the acceptance test). `tsc` is clean.
- **C++**:
  - `agent_bridge_tests`: 446 cases pass, with new tests for an optional purpose, plan-only calls, and the card's plan mark appearing and clearing.
  - `shell_theme_tests` passes.
  - `brand_tokens_tests` passes; its only failures are the two `[!shouldfail]` cases.
- **Prompt tests**: `test_steps.py` has 50 passing tests, including a new offline check of the opening cap (`opening_shape`). No live-model run was made.
- **Live in the built app**: the shell harness `--setup-differences-capture` ran on the Mac with its stand-in agent: `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`. Pictures are in `setup-card-two-part-pictures/`:
  1. A 3MF opened with no purpose: facts only, plus the "Opened card-opened.3mf as a new project" line.
  2. Purpose and plan recorded: "Stop the corners lifting", the headline, the rule, "… · 5 settings changed", and the estimates.
  3. After a person's File › Import: "Plan needs another look · Import Object: 20mmbox-LF.stl".

  The extra picture shows the mark after a hand edit. The run also shows that re-recording only the headline clears the mark and keeps the purpose.

## Not verified, and choices to check

- **Not run live:**
  - No real model has been run against the new skills, either for the 80-word cap or for re-recording the plan after an import. That needs Kenneth's approval for a batch.
  - The device-material annotation, saved cards, and the Undo and restore marks are covered by vitest or Catch2 only.
  - Windows and Linux were not tested.
- **Plan-mark reason**: shown exactly as the host stores it ("Import Object: …"), not in the canvas's illustrative wording.
- **Prompt recording**: `requests.json` is still the Windows recording from 2026-10-25, with the four new skill texts spliced in from a fresh macOS recording. Taking the whole macOS recording would shift the inputs the stored baseline was measured on. The prompt-test README records this.
- **OrcaSlicer behaviour**: its `load_files(std::vector)` takes no undo step. Agent tools load that way on purpose (their own edits don't mark the plan). The harness therefore imports with `add_model`, File › Import's call.
- **Design choices made without a decision:**
  - The card drops the user-confirmed material mismatch.
  - There is no All settings link when there is no agent or no settings were read.
  - "as a new project" is omitted when the note is not the chat's first message.
  - The calibration "test steps lost" note annotates the plan line, and the plan mark takes priority over it.
- **Truncation**: at the pane's default width, "5 settings changed" is cut to "5 settings chan…" (picture 2). The full text is in the tooltip. This may need a design look.

The implementation session is done. Its work is commit 0e59bd287c on the branch `claude/setup-card-two-part`, cut from jusprin-newui and not pushed; its report says it merges cleanly onto the current tip. Its worktree is at `.claude/worktrees/setup-card-two-part` with the report and four pictures untracked at its root. I read the report and looked at the three pictures, and they match the canvas boards.

**What it built.** The card in two parts, with the plan's validity now sent to the card, and the old states removed. The setup_record tool takes a plan without a purpose and its description says the headline is how, never what for. Both skills tell the agent to re-record the plan when the app has marked it. The file-loaded skill caps the opening message at about 80 words, two bullets and one question. A file opened as a new project draws the "Opened … as a new project · you · 09:53" line; an import draws nothing. The docs it updated: the design-system doc, the product definition, the architecture doc's opening-files section, the tool extension guide, and the code comments that described the old card.

**What passed.** Vitest with the wording guard, the bridge tests with new cases for the optional purpose and the plan mark, the theme and token guards, and the offline prompt tests with a new check of the opening message's shape. The shell harness ran the built app on the Mac through the three states.

**What was not verified, from its report.** No live model was run against the new skills, so the message cap and the re-record rule are untested with a real agent; that needs your approval for a batch. The device-material annotation and the saved cards are covered by unit tests only. Windows and Linux were not built.

**Two things to look at.** At the pane's default width the facts line cuts to "5 settings chan…" when the filament name is long; the full text is in the tooltip, but it may want a design answer. And in the third picture the "Previous estimates · not current" row shows no Recompute link, though the harness text says the link is present; worth a glance in the app before merging.

The session also made four small choices without a decision from you, listed at the end of its report: the user-confirmed material mismatch is dropped from the card, there is no All settings link when no agent is configured, "as a new project" is omitted when the note is not the chat's first message, and the calibration lost-steps note annotates the plan line below the plan mark.

The design-system scope question from my last message is still open: write the rule first and apply it to all the compositions, or move PinnedSetupCard out alone.

input.text:
Checked against the app's pane widths (design-tokens.json, component.agentPane: default 429 px, minimum 320 px; the card's inner width is 32 px less). Text measured in HarmonyOS Sans at the card's type roles.

At the default 429 px, one field truncates: the facts line, because it shares its row with the All settings link (316 px left for the text). With a Bambu preset name and a change count it overflows: "0.20mm Standard · Bambu PLA Basic · 5 settings changed" by 6 px, "0.20mm Standard · Bambu PLA Basic +2 · 1 setting changed" by 18 px, "0.16mm Optimal · Bambu PLA Matte +3 · 12 settings changed" by 27 px. Without a count, or with the canvas's "Gray PETG", it fits. Everything else fits at 429: a 59-character purpose takes 415 px of the 794 px two lines allow; the plan headline, the three annotations and the metrics row wrap or are short; the "Opened petg-pla+support+interface.3mf as a new project · you · 12:31" line fits with 19 px to spare.

At the 320 px minimum the facts line truncates with almost any count (by 80 to 136 px) and the opened-file line loses the end of the filename (by 19 to 90 px); the purpose, plan, annotations and metrics still fit.

So the one field that is cut by default is the facts line, and it is cut exactly when it carries the most information. Options:
1. Let the facts text wrap to two lines, the same two-line clamp the purpose has, with All settings staying top-right on the first line. The card grows 16 px only when needed. My pick: one rule for both text slots, nothing moves.
2. Put the change count on its own line under the presets ("5 settings changed"), always. Never truncates, costs 16 px on every card that has changes.
3. Shorten the words ("5 changed") and keep one line. Saves about 40 px; the Bambu "+2" cases still overflow at 320.

The opened-file line at 320 px I would leave: the tooltip holds the full name, and 320 is the pane's floor, not its default.

If you pick 1 or 2, I redraw the Current Setup Card boards, the component and the screens, and tell the implementation branch (the app has the same one-line facts row today).

content.text:
Your "1" from the comment thread is applied and the thread is resolved. The facts line now wraps to two lines before it clips, with All settings held on the first line's baseline, on the canvas boards, in the design system's PinnedSetupCard, and in the app's stylesheet in the main checkout, where the stylesheet guard and the card's tests pass. That change is uncommitted.

**On a popover over the fact lines: I would not add one.** Three reasons.

- The reason to want one is gone. The only field that was cut by default was the facts line, and it now wraps. At the pane's 320 px minimum the native tooltip already carries the full text, and 320 is the floor, not the default.
- There is nothing for it to say that is not one click away. The candidates are the full preset names, the list of changed settings with their old and new values, and the plate type. All of that is exactly what the All settings panel shows, with its Changed filter, and the link to it sits on the same line. The timeline rows already list each change with who made it and when. A hover popover would be a third home for the same facts, and that is the kind of accretion you asked to stop.
- Hover is a weak affordance for a card that should be readable at a glance. It does not exist for keyboard or touch, it hides information behind a gesture nobody is told about, and it would be the only hover popover in the pane.

If you ever want more than the line says, the honest place is the line itself: a second fact line, not a layer over it. So far nothing has needed that.
Commit the facts-line stylesheet change on jusprin-newui.
